This page opens every instrument of the [Atlas](atlas.qmd), one by one, at the text its
map was built from. A law, a regulation, a guideline or a treaty is shown as a
consolidated document, with its books, titles, chapters and sections as headings, its
articles as paragraphs and its tables as tables, so that it can be read from the first
line to the last or entered at any article.

The search box finds an instrument by name or by abbreviation, and it ignores accents
and case, so that *constitucion* finds the Constitution. The buttons above the table
keep one collection only, a click on a column heading sorts the table by it and a
second click reverses the order, and a name opens the instrument. The outline on the
left follows the document, a fold hides the contents of a title or a chapter, and a
click on any entry goes to that place.

An article, an introduction, a table or the preamble is what the Atlas calls an
excerpt, the piece of text that it compares with the rest of the corpus. A heading and
a transitory article say little about how two instruments relate, so they are left
out, and the remaining ones are called compared excerpts. Each of them is marked in
the margin of the document with a thin rule and the word *Compared*, and it carries a
*Nearest texts* line. Opening it lists the five closest texts that live in other
instruments, each with its similarity as the Qwen3 Embedding 4B model measures it,
which is the *4B* option of the Atlas. A text that several instruments share appears
once, with the others named under it. Following a link opens that other instrument at
the excerpt in question, highlighted, and the browser's back button returns to where
the reading was.

Every instrument and every excerpt has an address, so that a link can point at it. An
address such as `instruments.html?c=leyes&k=ccf#art_1` opens the Federal Civil Code at
its first article.

The text is the consolidated snapshot of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation
from which the vectors were built, and its date is shown under the name of each
instrument. The documents themselves are not part of the site's source, being the
`atlas-instruments` release of the repository, which the publishing workflow downloads
and unpacks next to this page, and the page fetches one file only when an instrument is
opened. The Diario Oficial de la Federación remains the official source of legal text.

:::
